body:
They told us the road was still open. The map pinned beside the shopping list had already been changed in pencil, and the neighbor who came for water said the gate was locked.

I left room for a correction and carried the paper through the night. I left the date on the page and did not try to straighten the damaged edge. Someone else might remember the same afternoon.
title: The route on the kitchen copy — in the margin

body:
I counted everyone in the queue before I counted cars. The person carrying the list wrote down the cars first and ran out of room for the family walking behind them.

The last vehicle passed with space for the supplies but none listed for us. My family asked me to put the paper away with the bills. I kept it separate because the person involved might come back for it.
title: A place under the names — in the margin

body:
My brother stayed for the later vehicle because our aunt could not get into the first. Its time was written on the back of a lunch receipt. No driver at the next barrier knew of it.

I kept the older copy in a coat pocket while everyone else was told to use the new one. I had meant to save it only until someone could explain the difference. By then the ordinary work around us had stopped.
title: The second pickup time — in the margin

body:
The house was marked cleared while we were still packing. I put a square around the date on our own copy. We waited for someone to return and ask who was inside.

The youngest still asked whether the driver knew where we were. We compared what we had seen with what was written there. The second account omitted the small part that had frightened us.
title: Inside the crossed square — in the margin

body:
The woman at the gate read our names aloud and put us on a bus list. Another person came out with a new list and said the first bus had already taken us.

The pencil count did not change when the people standing beside me did. I left the date on the page and did not try to straighten the damaged edge. Someone else might remember the same afternoon.
title: A seat counted twice — in the margin

body:
A man in a vest promised to come back after he moved the first group. His pencil left an unfinished arrow on my paper. I kept the page when the rest of the notices were pulled down.

The person who had written the first directions could no longer be found. My family asked me to put the paper away with the bills. I kept it separate because the person involved might come back for it.
title: The return line — in the margin

body:
We followed the directions given at dawn and found a chain across the road. Someone had moved the crossing but left the old sign standing. My father had memorized its distance because he could not read the smaller print.

I left room for a correction and carried the paper through the night. I had meant to save it only until someone could explain the difference. By then the ordinary work around us had stopped.
title: After the barrier moved — in the margin

body:
The clerk counted the beds as if each held one person. My mother was sitting beside my sister, waiting for her to stand. On the posted total there was only one of them.

The last vehicle passed with space for the supplies but none listed for us. We compared what we had seen with what was written there. The second account omitted the small part that had frightened us.
title: A count made indoors — in the margin

body:
I sent a change of address with the driver who said he could cross. The parcel came back with the new address rubbed out. The note from my husband inside had never been opened.

I kept the older copy in a coat pocket while everyone else was told to use the new one. I left the date on the page and did not try to straighten the damaged edge. Someone else might remember the same afternoon.
title: The parcel that returned — in the margin

body:
I copied the first line because it included our street. The replacement left the street out but retained the same number of vehicles. We stood beside the mailbox until the engines were gone.

The youngest still asked whether the driver knew where we were. My family asked me to put the paper away with the bills. I kept it separate because the person involved might come back for it.
title: Two versions of the line — in the margin
